_readme: GAME CONTENT, DRAFT PENDING PRODUCER REVIEW (every name, line and title). The NPC dialogue layer (docs/design/area-zero.md and docs/design/grove.md "NPCs" (D2) — the two share this one file, per grove.md's reconciliation note): Npcs (NpcId, DisplayName, PortraitKey = an art-manifest key, '' = a placeholder portrait), Lines (LineId, NpcId, Conditions, Text, Priority; a scene's own lines carry scene:{SceneId} so the Grove's resolution never picks them; a Grove condition is kind:params, see Tutorial.NpcConditionKinds, built live from account state by Npc.NpcRules.BuildFacts) and Scenes (SceneId, Title, LineIds: an ordered run of lines a story location plays, regions.json FixedNodes SceneId). D2 adds: Requests (RequestId, NpcId, Conditions, ItemId, Count, RewardKind, RewardId, Text — a one-off ask for a Grove item, Grove.GroveItemInventory, fulfilled once via Npc.NpcRules.FulfillRequest) and SideStories (StoryId, NpcId, DisplayName, Chapters: ChapterId, Conditions, Text, RequestItemId, RequestCount, RewardKind, RewardId, LoreId, NextChapterId — an optional per-NPC chapter chain, never required for the main campaign, tracked in PlayerSave.Npc.SideStories) and Lore (LoreId, Title, Text — the dialogue layer's own small codex, a request's or a chapter's reward, separate from Grove's and discovery's). v1 cast: the Grove Keeper (Hearthglen's mentor, who now also tends the Grove hub), the Trader, the Wandering Scholar and Forest Folk. No combat power anywhere, no gold that buys power; a title is earned only through an achievement (AchievementKinds.SideStoryComplete), never a request or side-story reward directly — RewardKind decor/look is mechanically wired (CheckReward) but v1 content authors only lore and none, the same 'wire it, do not author it yet' stance grove-library.json took for look rewards. Validated by BeastCraft.Tutorial.DialogueValidator (content load and the EditMode tests). Tone: content-bible.md (warm, wonder first; nobody dies).

Lines.Text: There you are. I am the Grove Keeper; I have tended this shrine since before the old oak by the mill was an acorn.
Your beast chose you. That is how every Beastbinder begins: not with a leash, but with a promise.
Hold out your hand. There: a small mending light, your first binder art. You will never strike in a fight; you will keep your friends standing.
Take these Fury Draughts, for when a fight turns against you. And go gently: the hedgerows are restless, and the Gloam's shimmer has reached the far hedge.
Rest here a while. The lanterns keep the haze at bay.
The miller says the Seals are only an old story. They are not. One sleeps in Verdant Hollow, just past the ridge.
Your newest friends are keen to keep up. Sit with them a while, and they will stand as tall as your first.
You calmed it. See how the haze slipped off, and the creature wandered home, dazed but whole? That is your work now.
Verdant Hollow starts past this ridge, and the Gloam is thicker there. Some places lie off the path: explore, and the map will fill in.
When you need a quiet place, find me at the Grove. And listen for kinship stones in the wild: more beasts are waiting to meet you.
The wild remembers kindness. So do I.
The mossy glade is yours now. Sit a while; the moss keeps the warmth of every beast that has rested here.
The tide pool breathes with the sea, even this far inland. Watch how the light moves across it at dusk.
The snow hollow never quite melts, and never quite freezes either. A patient sort of place.
You have started to make this place your own. A lantern here, a bench there, and it shows.
Six pieces placed with care, and the Grove already feels lived in. Beasts notice that more than you would think.
Whichever of your beasts has been keeping you company, it trusts you a little more than it did.
That bond has grown deep. Some beasts start humming old tunes at that stage. Have you noticed?
Five varieties in the herbarium already. The Wildgarden rewards patience more than skill.
Fifteen varieties pressed and catalogued. You could open a stall of your own at this rate.
That little tale a gift carried, I remember hearing it myself, long before you arrived.
Word travels fast from the wilds. I hear the first stretch of the road is calm behind you now.
Wares from every corner I have walked. Have a look, if coin or curiosity moves you.
A mossy glade for a home base, sensible. Easy to find, easy to defend, easy to sell to.
A tide pool habitat. I have seen beasts fetch salt glass from those on their own, given time.
A snow hollow keeps preserves fresher than any cellar I have paid for. Handy, that.
That sunwash dye in your pack, mixed well. Whoever crafted it has a good eye for warmth.
Ten varieties pressed already. I could move those at three markets before midday.
Twenty varieties now. You are outpacing half the growers I deal with on the road.
Whispering Hollow, was it. I have heard that story told three different ways by three different travellers.
The road past the first stretch is quieter now, they tell me. Good for business, good for you.
Two stretches of road cleared. I might finally take the long route again myself.
That beast of yours watches you the way a good pack mule watches its favourite handler. Rare, that.
You heard the start of my old road story, then. There is more to it, when you have the time.
You have heard the whole of my roads now, start to finish. Not many sit still long enough for that.
Every corner of this Grove is worth a footnote, if you look closely enough.
A mossy glade. The moss itself is worth studying, it only grows where a beast has slept undisturbed.
A tide pool this far from open water. I have three theories and no proof for any of them yet.
A snow hollow that never fully thaws. My notes on it already run to four pages.
Five varieties catalogued. The cross pollination patterns alone could fill a chapter.
Fifteen varieties now. Your herbarium is becoming more thorough than my own field notes.
Thirty varieties. I may need to ask you to review my next manuscript before I publish it.
That story about the phoenix bond, I have heard three tellings, and yours matches the oldest one.
Frostglass Ridge again. Every party that returns from there brings back a slightly different account.
The first stretch of road, quiet at last. I might finally survey it properly.
Your phoenix trusts you deeply now. Its plumage shifts a little at that stage, did you notice?
My atlas of this Grove is complete, thanks to you. I could not have mapped it half so well alone.
The wild has its own quiet ways. Stay a while and you will learn to hear them.
The glade hums when it is happy. Can you hear it yet? Most cannot, at first.
The tide pool remembers every beast that has ever drunk from it. Odd, but true.
The snow hollow keeps its own kind of warmth, underneath. Dig a little and you will feel it.
One little piece placed, and already the clearing feels less empty. Small things matter here.
Five pieces now. The wild things have started treating this place as part of the forest proper.
Your beast leans toward you now, just a little, when you are near. That is how it always starts.
That bond is about as deep as they come. Whatever you did, keep doing it.
That bark from the hollow, press it flat and dry, and it keeps its shape for years.
The road behind you is calmer now. The wild things feel it too, in their own way.
That bloom you brought me carried more of a story than you knew. Glad it found its way to me.
You calmed one of them with a gift instead of a fight. The Gloam lifts just as well for kindness as for courage.

Requests.Text: Bring me a vial of sunwash dye and I will tell you where I learned to spot a fair market from a rigged one.
Two ashbloom blossoms, if the Wildgarden has spared them. I want to check something about this soil.
A clear ice shard from Frostglass Ridge would settle an argument I have been having with myself for years.
A dewgrass bloom, freshly grown. The wild things ask for one every season, and I never say no.
Is that a duskrose phoenix I see? I would love an amber vial too, if you can spare one, to compare the dyes.

Chapters.Text: Sit with me a while. I want to tell you how this glade came to be the Grove's first root.
Bring me two sunpetal blooms, grown here and not bought elsewhere. I want to show you something about trust.
A vial of sunwash dye, if you have crafted one. The colour matters less to me than the making of it.
You have grown, gathered and given more than most who pass through here. That is the whole of the story, really.
I am mapping every habitat in this Grove, in my own slow way. Would you help me start with the snow hollow?
A frostfern bloom for my notes, if the Wildgarden has one ready. I suspect it only grows where the hollow's chill reaches.
A frost rose from the ridge would confirm a theory I have been chasing for three seasons now.
With the road behind you quiet, I can finally cross reference my notes against what you have seen out there. Thank you for your patience.
Settle in, and I will tell you how I ended up walking these roads instead of settling on one of them.
A vial of duskrose dye, if your Wildgarden has one to spare. It fetches a fair price where I am headed next.
Two stretches of road behind you now, same as me all those years ago. That is where this story ends, and a new one starts.

Lore.Title: The First Root
Lore.Text: Long before the habitats had names, the Grove Keeper planted a single seed here and waited three winters to see what it would become.

Lore.Title: A Question of Trust
Lore.Text: The Keeper says a beast's trust is grown the same way a garden is, slowly, and never by pulling on it to make it faster.

Lore.Title: Colour and Care
Lore.Text: Every dye the Wildgarden yields carries a little of the hand that mixed it, the Keeper claims to recognise a crafter by their sunwash alone.

Lore.Title: What the Grove Remembers
Lore.Text: The Keeper believes a Grove remembers every visitor who ever tended it, long after the visitor has forgotten the visit.

Lore.Title: Mapping the Cold
Lore.Text: The Scholar's notes on the snow hollow fill four pages and still end with the words more study needed.

Lore.Title: A Bloom Out of Season
Lore.Text: Frostfern only opens where a chill lingers past its season, the Scholar suspects the snow hollow keeps its own private winter.

Lore.Title: The Ridge Secret
Lore.Text: A frost rose, the Scholar explains, only forms where the ridge's wind crosses itself exactly right, proof, finally, of a theory chased for years.

Lore.Title: The Completed Page
Lore.Text: With the first stretch of road surveyed, the Scholar's atlas gains its first fully finished page, dedicated, in small handwriting, to a patient companion.

Lore.Title: Why I Walk
Lore.Text: The Trader once tried to settle in a single town and lasted one season before the road called again, some people are built for moving.

Lore.Title: The Duskrose Trade
Lore.Text: Duskrose dye fetches its best price three towns over, the Trader says, where the evenings run long and everyone wants a warmer colour to wear.

Lore.Title: Two Stretches Down
Lore.Text: The Trader admits that clearing two stretches of road, the same as their own first journey, feels less like an ending and more like finally being caught up to.

Lore.Title: Reading a Market
Lore.Text: The Trader learned to spot a fair market from a rigged one by watching which stalls the local children lingered near.

Lore.Title: What the Soil Holds
Lore.Text: The Grove Keeper tests ashbloom soil by scent alone, and claims to have never once been wrong about what grew there before the Grove did.

Lore.Title: A Clear Answer
Lore.Text: The clear ice shard confirms it, Frostglass Ridge's ice forms in perfect layers, one season at a time, like the slowest journal in the world.

Lore.Title: A Seasonal Gift
Lore.Text: The wild things bring dewgrass blooms to Forest Folk every season, and every season Forest Folk passes a few along to whoever seems to need one most.

Lore.Title: A Study in Dye
Lore.Text: The Wandering Scholar keeps a small book of pressed petals beside every dye vial, matching colour to colour until the pages run out.
